findings.problem: fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap() panics on any I/O failure (missing file, permissions, disk error)
findings.failure_mode: untrusted file paths cause process abort instead of returning a typed I/O error
findings.fix: Return Result<Vec<Record>, SessionError> and propagate fs::read_to_string with map_err to a typed I/O error variant

findings.problem: parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() panics on non-numeric input or out-of-range values
findings.failure_mode: malformed CSV lines abort the entire session load instead of returning a typed parse error
findings.fix: Use map_err to return a typed ParseError with the line context, do not unwrap parse results

findings.problem: lossy as u16 cast from u32 parse result silently truncates values above 65535
findings.failure_mode: a valid u32 like 70000 silently becomes 34464, corrupting domain data with no error signal
findings.fix: Use u16::try_from(parsed_u32).map_err(|_| ParseError::ValueOutOfRange) to reject values outside u16 range

findings.problem: parts[0] accesses the vec by index without bounds check
findings.failure_mode: a blank line or single-field line causes a panic via out-of-bounds indexing instead of a typed error
findings.fix: Use split_once(',') and destructuring to avoid indexing; bind (name, rest) = line.split_once(',').ok_or(Error::Malformed)

findings.problem: parts[1] accesses the vec by index without bounds check
findings.failure_mode: a line with only one comma-separated field causes a panic via out-of-bounds indexing
findings.fix: Destructure the second field from split_once instead of indexing parts[1]

findings.problem: println!("loaded {}", parts[0]) puts console I/O inside the data-processing closure
findings.failure_mode: I/O leaks into calculation logic, making the function non-deterministic, non-testable, and side-effectful where pure data transformation is required
findings.fix: Remove all println! from the parsing/calculation path; move logging/metrics to the shell layer that calls load_sessions

findings.problem: load_sessions fuses file I/O (fs::read_to_string), console I/O (println!), parsing, and domain construction into a single function
findings.failure_mode: pure parsing and calculation logic is mixed with shell I/O, violating the Data/Calculations/Actions architecture; impossible to unit-test the parsing without real files, impossible to suppress side effects
findings.fix: Split into: (1) a pure parse_session_line(&str) -> Result<Record, ParseError> for calculations, (2) an action shell load_sessions that reads the file, iterates lines through the parser, and collects results with bounded allocation

findings.problem: line.split(',').map(...).collect() into Vec<String> allocates unboundedly with no domain cap or try_reserve
findings.failure_mode: a file with millions of lines causes unbounded heap allocation and potential OOM with no graceful error
findings.fix: Validate a domain cap (max_rows) first, allocate Vec::new(), call values.try_reserve(max_rows).map_err(|_| Error::Allocation)?, then push parsed records one at a time with per-row cap enforcement

findings.problem: raw String primitives from split and parse cross the parse boundary without fallible smart constructors; callers can construct invalid domain states directly
findings.failure_mode: name is an unvalidated String and value is a potentially truncated u16 — no domain invariants are enforced at construction, so invalid records (empty names, out-of-range values) silently enter the system
findings.fix: Use split_once(',') at the boundary, parse value with try_from into a validated newtype, and construct Record only through a smart constructor that enforces name non-empty and value in-range

findings.problem: No typed error type exists; all failures are collapsed into panics via unwrap()
findings.failure_mode: consumers cannot distinguish I/O errors, parse errors, validation errors, or allocation failures — every failure is a process abort
findings.fix: Define a SessionError enum with variants: Io(io::Error), Malformed(usize, String), Parse(usize), OutOfRange(usize, u32), TooMany, Allocation. Return Result<Vec<Record>, SessionError>

findings.problem: Record stores name as raw String and value as raw u16 — both are primitives with no domain invariants encoded in the type
findings.failure_mode: any code can create Record { name: String::new(), value: 99999 } without validation, making illegal states representable
findings.fix: Use newtypes: Name(String) with a smart constructor enforcing non-empty, and Value(u16) with a smart constructor enforcing range; or use an enum with validated variants

findings.problem: line.split(',').map(...).collect() splits and allocates the entire line into a Vec<String> when only two fields exist
findings.failure_mode: unnecessary intermediate allocation on every line, plus the Vec loses the original line context needed for error reporting
findings.fix: Use line.split_once(',').ok_or(Error::Malformed) to split exactly once into (_name, value_str) pairs without intermediate Vec allocation

no profiler evidence for allocation hot path
no allocation tracking (e.g., custom allocator or profiling) for bounded allocation claims
no second-ring evidence for any zero-cost or performance claims
no command evidence (cargo fmt, cargo check, cargo clippy, cargo test) was run
no benchmark/baseline for stated or implied performance characteristics
residual_risk: Static review only — no commands were run. All 12 findings are BLOCKER-level violations of absolute Holzman Rust laws. The source contains unwrap (2), lossy as cast (1), unchecked indexing (2), hidden I/O (1), unbounded allocation (1), missing parse boundary (1), missing typed errors (1), raw primitive domain state (1), and incorrect separator parsing (1). The crate does not compile to safe Holzman standards. Repair required before any delivery gate.
